newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma says 92-96 privatisation broke law.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma says 92-96 privatisation broke law.

text.p: Russia's communist-dominated State Duma lower house of parliament attacked the government over its privatisation record on Thursday saying the cabinet had broken the law privatising state assets worth billions of dollars.

The Duma, which cannot issue binding orders to the government, overwhelmingly backed a draft bill saying the government's bold privatisation campaign in 1992-1996 was unsatisfactory and calling the cabinet to correct its mistakes.
The chamber is expected to pass the draft finally next week after considering amendments proposed by the deputies.
"The country suffered considerable losses from the privatisation of state and municipal property at give-away prices," the bill read, adding the process had broken the law.

The privatisation process, originally led by current reform chief First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, was heavily criticised for perceived insider dealing and low prices, but no major privatisations have been reversed.
Russian officials expect to raise 10-15 trillion roubles for the budget from privatisation this year.
